title: GEM: A Dataset of Engine Version Migrations in Open-Source Game Projects (v0.1)
description:
GEM records engine version state and migration events in open-source game projects. Godot is the instrument; the phenomenon is API evolution and breaking-change migration, and the version-extraction rule sits behind an adapter interface that admits Unity and Unreal without a schema change.

v0.1 covers a frame of 39,553 non-fork GitHub repositories created before Godot 4.0-stable, of which 5,988 were probed for their declared engine version and 300 were cloned and mined commit by commit. It contains 16 JSONL tables mirrored as CSV, plus captured pre- and post-migration trees for 103 repositories: 1,134 version events (131 major migrations), 135 migration windows with churn separated by file extension, 405 survival records reported under two reference versions rather than one, 327 demand and counter-demand signals, and a 200-repository instrument-agreement study.

Every row carries an ev_id naming the content-addressed artifact it was computed from, so each figure is re-derivable from a stored response rather than from a re-run of the collection. See SCHEMA.md for the 16 tables and the join graph, METRICS.md for every reported quantity and its definition, and DATASHEET.md for the Gebru-style datasheet including known limitations.
notes: Built with the GEM miner, archived separately under Apache-2.0. GitHub search result counts used during collection are approximate, include forks, and drift between runs; see DATASHEET.md for the standing caveat registry.
